title: Where does a bulb's power go?
hook: An old 60 W bulb lights a room. How much of its 60 W actually comes out as light?

knows: bulbs are sold by watts (60 W, 9 W)
doesNotKnow: the watt as energy per second
efficiency: the share of the input that ends up as the useful output
that energy in equals energy out, so what is not light is heat

misconception: A bulb turns nearly all its electricity into light.
objective: The learner can explain that a bulb's input power all leaves as light plus heat, that a filament bulb turns only about 5% into visible light, and that an LED gives the same light for far less input and far less heat.

claims.text: A watt (W) is one joule of energy per second.
claims.source: SI derived unit: 1 W = 1 J/s (BIPM SI Brochure, 9th ed., Table 4).

claims.text: Energy is conserved: all the power going into a bulb leaves as visible light plus heat.
claims.source: First law of thermodynamics for a device in steady state: power in = power out. 'Heat' here includes invisible infrared radiation and warmth carried off by the air and the fitting.

claims.text: A 60 W filament bulb turns about 5% of its power into visible light (about 3 W); the other 57 W leave as heat.
claims.source: Typical estimate, to be sourced by the verifier: incandescent radiant efficiency in the visible band is roughly 2-5% (US DOE Energy Saver, 'Incandescent lighting'; Wikipedia 'Luminous efficacy' table gives 1.9-2.6% luminous efficiency for 40-100 W tungsten bulbs, which counts eye-weighted light and is lower than the radiant visible share). 60 x 0.05 = 3 W, 60 - 3 = 57 W.

claims.text: A 9 W LED bulb gives about the same light as a 60 W filament bulb, so about a third of its input (3 W) is light and about 6 W is heat.
claims.source: Typical estimate, to be sourced: US DOE / ENERGY STAR equivalence of an 800 lumen LED (8-10 W) to a 60 W incandescent; white-LED wall-plug radiant efficiency roughly 30-40%. 9 - 3 = 6 W; 3 / 9 = 33%.

claims.text: The LED gives the same light for less than a sixth of the filament bulb's power.
claims.source: 9 / 60 = 0.15, less than 1/6 = 0.167 (figures from c3 and c4).

claims.text: A filament bulb makes light by heating a thin wire until it glows white hot; an LED makes light directly in a semiconductor.
claims.source: Incandescence (thermal emission from a hot tungsten filament, about 2,700 K) vs electroluminescence in a semiconductor diode: US DOE Energy Saver, 'Lighting Choices to Save You Money' and 'LED Lighting'.

recall.question: A 100 W filament bulb turns about 5% of its power into light. Roughly how much heat does it give off each second?
recall.why: Power in equals power out: 5 W leaves as light, so the other 95 W, 95 joules each second, leaves as heat.
